1471. 7. März. Krumau. — Der Pfarrer Johann von Rosenberg und die gesummte Bürgerschaft ebendaselbst schliessen mit Wissen und Willen des Johann von Krumau, Administrators des Prager Erzbisthums, und des Abtes Thomas von Hohenfurt einen Vertrag über ihre gegenseitigen Leistungen hin sichtlich der neu zu errichtenden Kaplanei bei der Rosenberger Pfarrkirche.

CCLX. In dei nomine amen. Quia scriptum est, dum tempus habemus operemur bonum, vt veniente tempore messis ex terreno semine frurtus in celestibus colligere valeamus perpetuos. Quod nos Johannes plebauus et magister ciuium consules jurati ac tota communitas ciuitatis Rosmberk aure cordis attendentes, cupientes ob augmentum cultus diuine ac ministrorum ecclesie in ßosnberk bonorum operum participes fieri, et nobis et aliis Christi fidelibus, qui ad infrascripta sua nobis sunt largiti, subsidia pro temporalibus celestia cumulare, ad honorem et landein dei omnipotentis et sue matris beatissime virginis Marie ac omnium sanctorum et precipue ad beati Nicolai confessoris ecclesie nostre patroni gloriosi gloriam sempiternam nee non ob remedium animarum nostrarum ac omnium predecessorum nostrorum et ad redimenda peccata omnium viuorum et mortuorum nobis ad hoc suffragantium matura et preuia deliberatione et de voluntate ac consensu reuerendi patris domini Johannis de Crumlow decani ecclesie et administratoris archiepiscopatus Pragensis com- missarii fidei ac decretorum doctoris et venerabilis patris domini Thome abbatis Altiuadeusis collatoris et patroni dicte ecclesie talem insimul fecimus concordiam: In primis quod quolibet die dominico aut alio quocumque die festiuo celebri missa cantata maturo tempore, que alias matura apellatur, de beata virgine Maria secundum tem- poris qualitatem cantetur, et quod qualibet feria secunda similiter cantata pro animabus benefactorum defunctis teneatur, nisi esset dies. Celebris impedimento, et tune alio die feriali competenti predicta missa defunctorum cantando suppleatur; quam missam presbyter cautans petitionem faciet pro animabus illis, que huic pio operi manus adiutrices porrexerunt, generalem. Item quod quolibet alio die feriato in septimana missa maturo tempore lecta habeatur, his diebus infrascriptis dumtaxat exceptis videlicet in uatiuitate domini epiphanie resurrectionis dominice ascensionis Christi penthccostes corporis Christi anunciationis purificationis visitationis assumptions 324 sanete Marie virginis omnium sanctorum et die animarum omnium. Sed considerans ego Jobannes plebanus predictus, quod vnus pres byter aut capellanus de nouo fundandus non possit omni die predictas missas pro voto communitatis explere ac quotidianus in diuino obse quio misse mature propter impedimenta canonica esse bonus pre- tactum, super me et omnes successores meos ex voluntate et assensu superiorum meorum modo infrascripto assumpsi et diuisi ad preces ciuium et comunitatis predicte: quod ego et omnes successores mei capellanum specialem debeo et debent deputare et disponere eique in dote cameram assignare, expensas ministrare et pro labore suo satisfacere et cum eodem componore. Qui capellanus ad tres missas in septimana erit obligatus, hoc est, die dominica ad vnam cantatam eria quarta ad secundam et feria sexta ad terciam lectas, et hoc si his duobus diebus ultimis erit feria, sed si his diebus duobus erit festum celebre, tune ¡idem (sic) capellanus tenebitur ad cantatas. Etiam iidem capellanus ad prefatas tres missas ordinatus vesperis matutinis processioni misse quolibet die dominico aut alio festiuo similiter et in diebus rogationum processioni et in vesperis defunc- torum, vbi agitur communis memoria'omnium animarum, debet et ftenetur presens interesse, et jura mea et successorum meorum ple- banorum vt offertoria testamenta quecunque non debet pro se vsur- pare, sed cum illis omnibus ad me et successores meos respectum habere et mihi dare, nisi ex gratia velim ex predictis Juribus aliquid eidem erogare. Residuis autem quatuor diebus in septimana mei et successorum meorum vicarii duo, quos ex antiqua consuetudine seruare debeo, in curia mea missas quatuor, siue leete siue cantate, ut predicitur, euenerint, implere debent, cum quibus vicariis et cum rectore schole concordare debeo pro eorum laboribus satis faciendo , modo quocumque meliori sciuero et potero. ítem domini ciues predicti e conuerso mihi meisque successoribus capellano et vicariis prefatis debent lumen, quod hucusque dederunt tempore byemali et estuali, ad prefatas missas cantatas et lectas dare et tribuere. Etiam dielj domini ciues sine omni dilatione et quacunque recusatione mihi plebano et meis successoribus debent et tenentur quindecim sexagenas grossorum bone monete in terra currentis et recipientis eandem quolibet anno dare diuisim, in festo sancti Georgii martyris medietatem vnam et in festo sancti Galli medietatem alteram, et decem tinas siliginis etiam quolibet anno, siue siligo tune in bono 328 siue ¡n caro foro fuerit. Item domini ciues illos centum grossos minus sex grossis, quos mihi prius soluebant hucvsque pro secundo vicario seruando deputatos, hos adhuc mihi et meis successoribus soluere et dare debent ultra illas quindecim sexagenas grossorum. Et pro petitinnibus generalibus fidélium defunctorum predictis etiam dicti domini ciues vltra predicta omnia etiam dare debent un grossos annuatim. �?ec etiam pena adiecta est, quod si missa cantata aliquo die predicto tenta non fuerit, tune duo grossi mihi et successoribus meis deperire debent, si autem lecta, tune vnus grossus tantum. Et hee littere concordie inter nos plebanum et ciues predictos tam diu debent su um firmamentum et robur obtinere, quam diu census liber per pretatos dominos ciues non erit dispositus pro capellania pre- dicta. In quorum omnium fidem et robur firmius predictorum nos Johannes plebanus et totum commune ciuitatis predicte sigilla nostra his litteris beniuole et de certa nostra sciencia appendimus. Et ut maior fides adhiberetur, etiam predictis prefatos reuerendos patres dominum Johannem decanum et administratorem etc. et dominum Thomam abbatem etc. necnon et famosum clientem dominum Johan nem dictum Sudek de Dluha petiuimus, vl sigilla eorum etiam his litteris appenderent et hanc concordiam munirent. Datum et actum Crumlow anno domini millesimo quadringentesimo septuagesimo primo die S. Thème de Aquino, que fuit septima Marcii. Fünf, an Pergamentstreifen hängende zum Theile stark beschädigte Sie gel. a) Ziemlich gross, in rothem Wachs. — St. Wenzl. — 'j- Sigillvm. Vica- riatYS . . . Pragensis. Als Gegensiegel in weissem Wachs: ein der Quere nach getheilter viereckiger Schild mit einer fünfblättrigen Rose über dem selben. Keine Legende. b) Ebenso. In einer gothischen Capelle mit Stab und Buch, stehend; am Postament zwei Schilde mit Rosen. — Sigillvm . Thome. Abbatis . In . Alto . Vado. c) Klein, schlecht in schwarzem Wachs abgedruckt- Ein Schild mit einem Hunde? — S . Yan . Z . Dlvhe. d) In grünem Wachs, guldengrose. — St. Nikolaus. — ... In. Rosenberg. Dieses und das folgende Siegel haben auch ein Gegensiegel, das leider schlecht abgedruckt ist. Das Brustbild eines Mannes, der in den Händen eine Capelle oder Thürmchen zu halten scheint, rechts ein i und links ein b? Ohne Legende. e) Ziemlich gross, in grünem Wachs. — Ein Schild mit einer Rose. — S. Civitatis . De . Rosenberch. 326
entries.english:
1471, 7 March. Krumau. — The parish priest Hans von Rosenberg and the entire citizenry there, with the knowledge and consent of Johann von Krumau, administrator of the Prague archbishopric, and Abbot Thomas of Hohenfurt, conclude an agreement concerning their respective obligations in connection with the newly established chaplaincy at the Rosenberg parish church.

CCLX. In the name of God, amen. It is written: “While we have time, let us do good,” so that when the harvest comes we may gather everlasting fruits in heaven from the seed sown on earth. We, Johannes, parish priest, the sworn master of the citizens and councilors, and the whole community of the city of Rosenberg, have taken this to heart. Desiring to share in good works for the increase of divine worship and the ministers of the church at Rosenberg, and to heap up heavenly things for ourselves and for other Christian faithful who have given us the support set out below in exchange for temporal things, to the honor and praise of almighty God, his most blessed mother the Virgin Mary, and all the saints, especially for the everlasting glory of Saint Nicholas the Confessor, glorious patron of our church, and also for the remedy of our souls and those of all our predecessors, and for the redemption of the sins of all the living and dead who aid us in this, after mature and prior deliberation, and with the will and consent of the reverend father Lord Johannes of Krumau, dean of the church and administrator of the Prague archbishopric, commissioner of the faith and doctor of canon and civil law, and of the venerable father Lord Thomas, abbot of Hohenfurt, collator and patron of the said church, we have made the following agreement together.

First, every Sunday or other solemn feast day, an early sung Mass, otherwise called the early Mass, shall be sung in honor of the Blessed Virgin Mary according to the season. Every Monday likewise a sung Mass shall be held for the souls of deceased benefactors, unless prevented by a solemn feast day; in that case the said Mass for the dead shall be supplied by singing it on another suitable weekday. The priest celebrating that Mass shall make a general prayer for the souls of those who have lent a helping hand to this pious work.

On every other weekday of the week, an early read Mass shall also be held, except only on the following days: the Nativity of the Lord, Epiphany, the Resurrection of the Lord, the Ascension of Christ, Pentecost, Corpus Christi, the Annunciation, Purification, Visitation, and Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary, All Saints, and All Souls. But I, the aforesaid Johannes, parish priest, considering that one priest or newly founded chaplain could not celebrate all the Masses requested by the community every day, and that the early daily Mass could be impeded by canonical obligations, have, with the consent of my superiors, undertaken and arranged the following at the request of the citizens and community: I and all my successors must appoint and provide a special chaplain, assign him a room as his endowment, provide his expenses, pay him for his work, and make an agreement with him.

That chaplain shall be bound to celebrate three Masses each week: one sung Mass on Sunday, a second Mass on Wednesday, and a third on Friday, the latter two read; but if either of those two days is a solemn feast, the same chaplain must celebrate a sung Mass on that day. The chaplain appointed for these three Masses must also be present at Vespers, Matins, and the procession for Mass on every Sunday or other feast day, and at the procession on Rogation days and at Vespers for the dead, when a common commemoration of all souls is held. He must not appropriate to himself my rights and those of my successors as parish priests, including offerings and any testamentary bequests, but must defer to me and my successors in all these matters and hand them over to me, unless I choose to grant him something from those rights as a favor.

On the remaining four days of the week, my two vicars and those of my successors, whom I am bound to maintain according to ancient custom, must perform four Masses in my court, whether read or sung as described above. I must agree with those vicars and with the schoolmaster on suitable compensation for their work, in whatever way I know and can best arrange.

Furthermore, the aforesaid citizens must, in turn, continue to provide me and my successors, the chaplain, and the said vicars with the light which they have hitherto supplied in winter and summer for the said sung and read Masses. The citizens must also, without delay or refusal, pay me, the parish priest, and my successors fifteen sexagenae of good coin current and accepted in the land each year, in two installments: half on the feast of Saint George the Martyr and the other half on the feast of Saint Gall. They must also give ten tuns of rye each year, whether rye is then available in a good or dear market.

The citizens must further pay and give to me and my successors the one hundred minus six groschen which they have hitherto paid me, assigned for maintaining a second vicar; this is in addition to the fifteen sexagenae of groschen. For the general prayers for the deceased faithful mentioned above, the citizens must also give one groschen annually, in addition to all the foregoing.

A penalty is also stipulated: if a sung Mass is not held on any of the aforesaid days, two groschen are to be deducted from what is due to me and my successors; if a read Mass is missed, only one groschen is to be deducted. This agreement between us, the aforesaid parish priest and citizens, shall remain in force and valid for as long as the aforesaid citizens have not assigned a free rent for the said chaplaincy.

As firmer proof and confirmation of all this, we, Johannes, parish priest, and the whole community of the said city, have willingly and with full knowledge attached our seals to this charter. So that greater credence might be given to it, we also asked the reverend fathers named above, Lord Johannes, dean and administrator, and Lord Thomas, abbot, as well as the distinguished knight Lord Johannes called Sudek of Dluha, to attach their seals to this charter and confirm the agreement. Given and enacted at Krumau in the year of our Lord 1471, on the feast of Saint Thomas Aquinas, which was 7 March.

Five seals hang from parchment strips, partly badly damaged. (a) Rather large, in red wax: Saint Wenceslas; legend: “Seal of the Vicariate … of Prague.” As a counterseal, in white wax, a shield divided horizontally, with a five-petaled rose above it; no legend. (b) Likewise, a figure standing in a Gothic chapel with staff and book; two shields with roses at the base. “Seal of Thomas, Abbot in Hohenfurt.” (c) Small, poorly impressed in black wax: a shield with what may be a dog; “S. Yan. Z. Dlvhe.” (d) In green wax, a gold groschen: Saint Nicholas; “… in Rosenberg.” This and the following seal also have a counterseal, poorly impressed: a man’s bust apparently holding a chapel or small tower, with an i on the right and perhaps a b on the left; no legend. (e) Rather large, in green wax: a shield with a rose; “Seal of the City of Rosenberg.”
